albums.blurb: Snarky Puppy is a large-ensemble fusion collective led by bassist and composer Michael League, formed around the University of North Texas jazz program in Denton and drawing on a rotating cast of dozens of players. After building their reputation on albums tracked live in front of in-studio audiences, they made Culcha Vulcha at the isolated Sonic Ranch studio in far-west Texas — their first pure studio recording in nearly a decade — working West African, Latin, and Southern funk grooves into ten instrumentals.
albums.reception: Culcha Vulcha won the Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Instrumental Album at the 59th Grammy Awards in February 2017, the band's third Grammy.

albums.blurb: Vulfpeck is the Ann Arbor, Michigan minimal-funk outfit assembled by producer Jack Stratton, with Joe Dart's bass at its center. Thrill of the Arts was the band's first full-length after a run of EPs — and after 2014's Sleepify, the silent album fans streamed on loop until Spotify pulled it, whose royalties funded an admission-free tour. The record folds guest vocalists, including Antwaun Stanley and Blake Mills, into the group's stripped-down, pocket-first sound.
albums.reception: Thrill of the Arts debuted at number 16 on Billboard's R&B Albums chart.

albums.blurb: The Blue Nile were a famously unhurried trio from Glasgow, fronted by singer Paul Buchanan, who recorded for hi-fi manufacturer Linn's in-house label and released just four albums in more than two decades. Hats, their second, arrived six years after 1984's A Walk Across the Rooftops: seven long, meticulously built songs of synthesizers and drum machines under Buchanan's weathered voice, mostly about city lights, rain, and longing.
albums.reception: Hats reached number 12 on the UK Albums Chart — the band's best showing — and drew a rare five-star review from Q magazine on release.
